name: SURINAME
lead: Suriname is the smallest country in South America. Rainforest covers nine-tenths of it. Paramaribo is a UNESCO city of Dutch wooden houses. Creoles, Hindustanis, Javanese, Maroons and Indigenous peoples live side by side.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: About the size of Georgia, USA

sections.culture: A world in one city block
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Suriname sits on the Guiana Shield, one of Earth's oldest rocks. Thick forest covers most of the land, with granite mountains and dark rivers.
The Suriname, Marowijne and Coppename rivers drain the highlands. The Central Suriname Nature Reserve protects 16,000 km² of forest.
animals: The giant river otter is nearly 2 metres long. Families fish together on sandbanks and chatter loudly. Suriname's rivers are one of the last safe places for them.
Jaguars roam the deep forest. Tapirs, giant armadillos and eight kinds of monkey live here too. Over 700 bird species include the scarlet macaw.
culture: In Paramaribo, a mosque and a synagogue stand side by side. People have lived together peacefully for 300 years.
Food shows the mix. Roti and curry came from Hindustani cooks. Nasi goreng is Javanese. Pom is a Creole chicken dish.
history: The Lokono and Kalina peoples lived along the rivers first. In 1667, the Dutch gave England a small island called Manhattan. In return, they kept Suriname, then the world's richest sugar colony.

Enslaved Africans fled brutal plantations into the forest. They formed free Maroon nations and fought the Dutch to a standstill. Peace treaties came in the 1760s. Suriname became independent on 25 November 1975.
wows: In 1667, the Dutch gave up Manhattan (now New York) to get Suriname.
Suriname is the only South American country where Dutch is the official language.
Over 90% of Suriname is rainforest, one of the highest shares on Earth.
St. Peter and Paul Cathedral is the largest wooden building in the Western Hemisphere.
A mosque and a synagogue stand next to each other on Keizerstraat.
Julianatop was first climbed only in 1963. Its Amerindian name means 'He who stands alone.'
Gold makes up 79% of exports. About 20,000 small miners pan the rivers.

myths.myth: New York was always called New York
myths.fact: The Dutch named it New Amsterdam. England took it in 1664 and renamed it for the Duke of York.

myths.myth: Jaguars are the biggest cats on Earth
myths.fact: Tigers and lions are bigger. The jaguar is the biggest cat in the Americas, and its bite can crack turtle shells.
